subject: FinMate expansion — unit economics & volume step-up (post-demo recap)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sera Lawson <sera.lawson@finmate.io>, Markus Reed <markus.reed@finmate.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinMate expansion — unit economics & volume step-up (post-demo recap)

Hi Sera / Markus,

Great to meet you both on the call — thanks for walking through the FinMate roadmap and the three routes you plan to expand (authn prompts, customer support summarization, and credit-scoring reranks). Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can put together a clean renewal/expansion proposal: 

Summary from today:
- Current committed usage: ~3M tokens/month (inferred from your GA usage file)
- Target post-rollout: ~10–14M tokens/month within 3–6 months (main lift from support summarization)
- Primary constraint: monthly budget band target $10k–$18k (you mentioned $12k as ideal)

Pricing & unit economics items to confirm:
1) Target blended $/1M tokens you need for the committed portion vs. overages (you mentioned a target ballpark of $700–$900 / 1M) — can you confirm a firm target?
2) Which routes should be prioritized for dedicated capacity (reduces latency but changes pricing): authn prompts + credit-scoring reranks?
3) Do you want model-level isolation (e.g., pin credit-scoring to a small, quantized model variant) or route-level (same model, different pools)?

Next steps I propose:
- We’ll prepare a blended-tier proposal that shows: committed tiers (3M, 6M, 12M) with step-up discounts and a blended $/1M for your expected mix.
- Include a short appendix that models blended economics under your 3 growth scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive).
- If you confirm routes for dedicated capacity, we’ll include dedicated pool pricing and a canary rollout plan to limit risk.

Can you reply with: 1) an internal target $/1M (if you have a hard ceiling), 2) confirmation of which routes should be routed to Dedicated, and 3) whether you can share last 3 months of token-by-route usage (or confirm the spreadsheet we referenced)?

Attaching: FinMate_Monthly_Usage.xlsx (the file you uploaded to the call) — I’ll drop a proposal PDF once we have the target $/1M.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales \u2014 Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Ben 17:03 PST

Great recap. Quick answers below: 

1) Target $/1M: We're looking for something in the $750	600 / 1M range overall. For committed volume wed be comfortable around $800 / 1M if that includes prefix caching and a short KV cache retention for reranks. Overage bands should be higher (we expect occasional spikes).
2) Dedicated routes: please prioritize authn prompts and credit-scoring reranks for Dedicated. Support summarization can run on shared pools initially.
3) Model isolation: prefer route-level isolation (same model, different pools) for now. If the math is clearly better for pinning model variants we can discuss.

We uploaded the last 3 months (by route) to the sheet you attached — theres a new tab titled "Growth-Scenarios" with our expected monthly multiplier (x1.5 -> x4 over 6 months).

Budget constraint: our budget team has signaled a target of $12k/month for Q2 baseline, with the potential to expand to $16k-$18k if unit economics hit our internal target.

Attachment: FinMate_monthly_by_route.csv (uploaded)

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to run the blended numbers together.

Sera Lawson
Head of ML Platforms \u2014 FinMate
sera.lawson@finmate.io | +1 (617) 555-8877

Thanks for the fast turnaround, Sera. Based on the spreadsheet and your target, Ive sketched a few options (high level) — attaching the draft proposal and a tiny CSV with the blended math. Key points: 

Option A (Conservative commit):
- Commit: 3M tokens/mo at $950 / 1M
- Overage: $1,350 / 1M
- No Dedicated pools included; route-level routing on shared capacity

Option B (Step-up blend - recommended):
- Commit: 6M tokens/mo at $880 / 1M
- Step-up: 12M tokens/mo at $760 / 1M (applies to the incremental band)
- Blended $/1M (expected mix): ~$820 / 1M
- Dedicated pools for authn + reranks (adds dedicated premium of $0.12 / 1k tokens equivalent, rolled into blended calculation)

Option C (Aggressive + Dedicated):
- Commit: 12M tokens/mo at $720 / 1M
- Blended with overage protection: ~$760 / 1M
- Includes Dedicated pools for prioritized routes and a 30-day canary period

A few commercial notes: 
- We can offer a one-time renewal credit (10% of first-month invoice) if you sign before end of Q2.
- Dedicated routing requires a brief config window (2 business days) and a small migration fee for the private pool (listed in the attached proposal).

Next asks from us so we can finalize for legal: 
1) Confirm which option (A/B/C) you want to pursue or tell us a preferred committed tier.
2) Confirm acceptance of Dedicated routing for authn + reranks (yes/no).
3) Any procurement lead / PO number we should use once legal sends the SOW.

Attaching: redwood-proposal-v3.pdf, blended-pricing-calculator.csv

I'll set up a short 30-min pricing review with Priyom and Evelyn if you want to walk the math together. Connor, Priyom, Evelyn: pinging you for quick review of the pricing bands and dedicated premium (see attachment).

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise Sales \u2014 Redwood Inference

Ben / team,

Quick internal notes before we finalize: 
- Legal: fine with the structure but requests we avoid guaranteeing sub-100ms p95 latency on shared pools. Put latency SLO language into the Dedicated pool section only.
- Finance: recommends we limit the 12M anchor to a 9-12 month term to avoid long tail exposure for a high discount tier.
- Commercial: I support Option B as the best balance. If FinMate signs a 9-month ramp (6 -> 12M), we can commit to the blended $820 / 1M and include the 10% one-time renewal credit.

Ben: please update the proposal to reflect a 9-month ramp commitment for the 12M anchor and add a short canary ops runbook for Dedicated routing. Evelyn: can you add the proposed latency SLO language and the migration fee line item?
